plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The minimal width $N_c(w)$ is determined by the algebraic rank of the constraint matrix formed by the $w$ sample points in a sufficiently rich feature space (e.g., via Fourier or polynomial basis), such that $N_c(w) \ge \text{rank}(\Phi)$, and rigidity is achieved when the feature map is injective on the constraint set.

steps.description: Implement a numerical experiment to test the hypothesis that minimal width $N_c(w)$ is determined by the algebraic rank of the constraint matrix $\Phi$ formed by $w$ sample points in a feature space. The workflow will: (1) generate synthetic constraints using a known function $f(x)$; (2) construct the feature matrix $\Phi$ using Fourier/polynomial basis; (3) compute rank($\Phi$); (4) train small feedforward networks of varying widths on $w$ points; (5) evaluate max absolute error on held-out points; (6) identify $N_c(w)$ as the smallest width achieving zero violation (error $\le 10^{-3}$); and (7) compare $N_c(w)$ to rank($\Phi$) to verify if rigidity is achieved when the feature map is injective. All results will be logged with convergence status and error metrics.

plans.objective: [DIM: measure] The minimal width $N_c(w)$ is governed by the tail probability of the empirical risk distribution over random weight initialization; for a fixed width, the probability of achieving zero-violation scales as $1 - (1 - p)^{w}$ where $p$ is the probability that a single random initialization satisfies one constraint, and $N_c(w)$ is the smallest width such that this probability exceeds a threshold (e.g., 0.9).

steps.description: Design a numerical experiment to test the hypothesis on minimal width $N_c(w)$ for small feedforward networks. Define the constraint set (analytic functions), sample w constraints, train networks of varying width w, and measure the maximum absolute error on held-out constraints. Determine the smallest width achieving zero-violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3). Use a grid search over widths and constraint counts to identify if N_c(w) is finite and bounded (rigid) or unbounded (fat).

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The minimal width $N_c(w)$ is determined by the algebraic rank of the constraint matrix formed by the $w$ sample points, where $N_c(w) \geq \text{rank}(A)$ is necessary for zero-violation feasibility.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Write a Python script to numerically test the hypothesis by constructing constraint matrices from sample points, computing their algebraic ranks, and scanning network widths to measure empirical $N_c(w)$ for zero-violation feasibility. The script will compare $N_c(w)$ against $\text{rank}(A)$ to determine if the algebraic rank determines the minimal width.
